title: Failed AI-agent execution trace
description: One record per failed run. Every field carries an explicit visibility tier in `x-visibility`. VISIBLE = handed to the diagnostic agent for free at episode start. PROBE = revealed only by the named probe, at that probe's cost. HIDDEN = owned by the evaluator; never serialised into an Observation. The tiering here is the experiment: if it drifts, results stop being comparable.

task.description: The goal given to the failed agent.

final_result.description: What the agent ultimately returned. Present even when the run failed.

final_error.description: Surface error, if the run terminated with one. null for silent failures where the agent returned an answer that was simply wrong.

reference_trace_id.description: A known-good run of the same task. The diagnostic agent sees only whether one exists; its contents cost a compare_known_good probe.

summary.description: One-line header. Leakage rule L2: generated from kind and surface arguments only. Must never contain diagnostic prose.

plan_text.description: The agent's reasoning. Hidden because reading reasoning is exactly the expensive act being budgeted.

replay_record.description: Preserved external observation captured at trace time. null means replay is IMPOSSIBLE here, which is a distinct answer from 'replay agreed'.

name.description: Amendment A1 (2026-08-12): tool names are free. Every real tracing UI shows the call signature without further work.

arguments.description: Amendment A1: argument VALUES are free. Note this is evidence, not a label -- see README 'Evidence vs labels'. It does weaken schema-probe headroom; consequence recorded in research/discussion-record.md.

schema.description: The tool's DECLARED contract. Hidden: seeing an argument is not the same as knowing what the tool required. This is what schema validation actually costs you.

ground_truth.description: Evaluator-only. Never reachable from an Observation; enforced by an object-graph walk in tests/test_contract.py.

mechanism.description: True failure mechanism. PRIMARY prediction target.

family.description: Fine-grained fault family. Never predicted; used only for stratified error analysis and for the held-out H5 split.

root_cause_step.description: True failure step: the FIRST MEANINGFULLY WRONG step. SECONDARY prediction target.

crash_step.description: Where the failure surfaced. Deliberately NOT the prediction target; the gap between the two is what makes localization non-trivial.

in_taxonomy.description: false for held-out families. Escalation is then the only correct action.

distractor_steps.description: Innocent steps between root cause and crash. Each survives inspection cleanly.
